subject: Anchored rate + failure/fallover terms — request for exec authorization
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Anchored rate + failure/fallover terms — request for exec authorization

Team,

Quick summary and ask: Ellipse Health (HS-45821) is asking for a 3-year anchored rate (price lock) with a built-in uplift cap and a midterm reset clause tied to usage growth. They want these commercial protections formalized in the MSA before signing — procurement flagged it as a blocker for Q3 start.

Key commercials:
- Term: 36 months
- Anchor: 3-year price lock (apply to base per-token rates)
- Uplift cap: customer requires a maximum annual uplift cap (they proposed 8%)
- Midterm reset: they want a reset at 24 months if usage > 2x committed volume (they asked for downward/ upward reset language)
- Renewal protection: ability to preserve effective rate for first renewal if they meet usage thresholds

Why this is material: Ellipse is a strategic health-tech customer with strong references and likely expansion (>5M tokens/mo in year 2 under our model). Granting an overly generous uplift/exit mechanism creates multi-year revenue exposure; however, losing the deal is also a risk for our Q3 ARR plan.

Attached: Ellipse_MSA_v3.pdf (redlines from their counsel) and rate-model-ellipse.xlsx (forecast scenarios).

Request: Executive authorization to sign an exception that includes the following recommended guardrails (please confirm):
1) Approve 3-year anchor with a maximum uplift cap of 6% annually (fixed cap — not compounding).
2) Midterm reset allowed at month 24 only if usage > 250% of committed baseline; reset limited to market index + 2% (no downward resets below the anchor).
3) Renewal protection: preserve effective per-token rate for one renewal window only if customer meets or exceeds baseline consumption for preceding 6 months.
4) Require finance to sign off on any final language that affects revenue recognition (I will loop them).

If you approve, I will incorporate these conditions into the MSA redline and send for final legal and finance review. If you have alternate guardrails, please suggest.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.inference

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchored rate + failure/fallover terms — request for exec authorization

Thanks Priyom — good write-up. A couple quick operational clarifications before execs weigh in:

- Can you confirm committed baseline (monthly tokens) in the attached model? I want a clean number to tie the 250% threshold to.
- The "reset limited to market index + 2%" — which index are we referencing? Recommend we reference our published price index (internal) or CPI + 2% to be explicit.
- Also suggest we add a Clause: "Fallback SLA & failover" — if our hosted capacity is interrupted, we add a 30-day remediation window and temporary credit, but no unilateral price waiver. Keeps reliability exposures contained.

If Priyom can confirm numbers, I support the 6% uplift cap (vs the 8% they requested) and the month-24 hard reset only.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Deal Desk — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference

Appreciate the summary. My recommendation (given strategic signal and upside):

- Approve anchor for 36 months.
- Approve uplift cap at 6% annual (non-compounding). We should push back from 8%.
- Midterm reset: allow one-time reset at month-24 if usage > 250% baseline; reset to our then-current list rate but limited to nav-index + 2% (finance to confirm exact index mechanics). No downward adjustment below anchor.
- Renewal protection: allow rate hold for first renewal only if customer maintains >= 100% baseline for previous 6 months. After first renewal, treat as standard renewal (no special preservation).

Conditions:
1) Legal must include a specific "failure/fallover" remediation clause (Kim's suggestion): 30-day remediation, temporary service credit up to 5% of monthly invoice for qualifying outages; automatic fallback to compatible model variant if available (no long-term price concessions).
2) Finance to sign off on revenue recognition impact and the index definition (I'll ping them).

If Laura approves, Priyom move to accept these guardrails in the MSA redline and send to Ellipse counsel. We should also include a one-time non-refundable setup fee to offset onboarding costs (suggest $45k).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations

Thanks team — I reviewed the ask and Aditya's recommendations. I authorize proceeding under the following executive authorization (final conditions):

1) Approve 36-month anchor with uplift cap at 6% (non-compounding) — executive signoff granted.
2) Approve one midterm reset at month-24 only if usage > 250% of committed baseline (use the baseline in rate-model-ellipse.xlsx). Reset must be limited to our published price index + 2% (Kim/Finance: please confirm exact index name).
3) Renewal protection granted for the first renewal only if customer sustains >= 100% baseline for previous 6 months.
4) Include fallover/remediation language: 30-day cure period, temporary credit up to 5% monthly invoice for qualifying incidents; no price concessions tied to temporary capacity constraints.
5) Add a one-time non-refundable onboarding fee of $45,000 to the contract.
6) Legal and Finance to finalize exact MSA language and confirm revenue recognition; I want a short summary memo from Finance confirming there is no material revenue deferral risk.

Priyom: please prepare a clean MSA redline reflecting these terms and run it through Legal & Finance. Once Finance provides the memo, I will sign the exec authorization for Deal Desk to finalize.

Laura
Laura Bennett
